name: Capacity Planning Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday capacity planning work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical capacity planning tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday capacity planning work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical capacity planning tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen capacity planning approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. Keep capacity planning changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Validate capacity planning outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. State assumptions about capacity planning explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. When capacity planning guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to capacity planning (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Prefer explicit, readable capacity planning solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. When multiple capacity planning strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Check that capacity planning terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. When capacity planning decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
11. Prefer the simplest capacity planning approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
12. Keep capacity planning outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop capacity planning edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new capacity planning abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic capacity planning advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about capacity planning over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
